Fa (Flutter Agent Harness) · Effective date: October 15, 2026
English Русский

English

This policy covers the Fa applications — the mobile/desktop/web app and the Fa browser extension ("fa — browser agent") — built on the open-source Flutter Agent Harness. The short version: the products are designed local-first — your keys, chats, and files stay on your device, and content leaves the device only to the AI providers you explicitly connect.

1. Data we collect

Fa has no accounts and no sign-up. Depending on how you use it, the following data is handled by the app on your device:

  • Chat and conversation content you send through fa — your prompts, the agent's replies, and the conversation context.
  • Provider API keys you enter so fa can talk to your chosen AI provider (e.g. OpenRouter, Anthropic, or a custom endpoint).
  • Page content the agent reads when you ask it to act on a page (text, screenshots, cookies needed for the flow you drive, history/bookmark entries you explicitly reference).
  • Local files you attach or files the agent creates for you in its sandbox.
  • The developer receives none of the above. There is no telemetry or analytics in the browser extension at all; in the mobile/desktop app, optional Firebase analytics/crash reporting is described in section 2 and never includes message text, keys, or file contents.

2. How we handle data

  • On-device processing. Prompts, tool results, and files are processed on your device. Nothing is proxied through the developer: fa operates no servers that receive your conversation content, keys, or files.
  • AI requests. When you chat with the agent, the relevant prompt and context are sent — directly from your device — to the AI providers you configure (your keys, your base URLs). Those providers process your data under their own privacy policies.
  • Analytics (app only). Where the platform makes it available, the mobile/desktop app sends Firebase Analytics events with metadata only (event names, provider/model identifiers, coarse buckets) and Firebase Crashlytics crash reports (stack traces, device model, OS version) — never API keys, message text, prompts, or file contents. The browser extension sends no analytics and no crash reports.
  • Website analytics. The landing page (fa1.dev) uses Google Analytics 4 with IP anonymization to count page views and outbound clicks. It sets no advertising cookies and tracks nothing inside the app you run from the page.

3. Data storage

  • Everything fa keeps — chats, sessions, settings, provider keys, sandbox files — is stored locally on your device or in your browser: the platform Keychain / secure store for keys (app), chrome.storage and extension storage for extension state, OPFS/IndexedDB for web sandboxes and downloaded model caches.
  • Nothing is stored cloud-side by the extension or the developer. There is no fa account and no fa cloud.
  • On-device model files you choose to download (e.g. small LLM weights) are stored in your browser's storage and are never uploaded.

4. Data sharing

  • We do not sell your data, and we do not share it with third parties for marketing.
  • The only third parties that receive your content are the model providers you explicitly configure (your requests go directly to their endpoints).
  • Native messaging. When you pair the extension with a local fa CLI helper, the extension and that local helper exchange messages between themselves on your machine — this traffic does not involve the developer or any server.
  • Optional system permissions (notifications, microphone, calendar, contacts, health, home) are requested only in context for features you invoke, and the data they touch is processed on-device only.

5. Retention & deletion

  • Local data persists until you delete it: clear a chat/session inside the app, clear the extension's data via browser settings, or uninstall — uninstalling the app or extension removes its locally stored data.
  • Downloaded model weights and web-sandbox files live in your browser storage and can be cleared the same way (site data / extension data).
  • Firebase analytics/crash data (app only), where enabled, is retained per Google's standard Firebase retention and contains no message content.

6. Security

  • Keys. Provider API keys are stored in the platform Keychain (iOS/macOS) or the local secure store / browser storage of the app sandbox, and are transmitted only to the provider they belong to.
  • Redaction. A layered secret-redaction pipeline masks credentials and token-shaped strings in logs, session files, and tool output before they are persisted, so secrets do not leak into recorded sessions.
  • Approvals. Sensitive agent actions (running commands, opening pages, sending data out of the browser) pass an approval gate you control, from ask-per-action to fully unattended modes.
  • The extension loads all interpreter/LLM engine code from inside the package (no remotely hosted code), and its permissions are limited to what its features call.

7. Children's privacy

The app and the extension are not directed at children under 13 (or the equivalent minimum age in your jurisdiction), and we do not knowingly collect personal data from them.

8. Changes to this policy

Changes are posted at this URL with a new effective date.

  • October 15, 2026 — restructured into the nine Chrome Web Store mandatory sections; added the browser extension (local engine code, native messaging, no telemetry).
  • July 29, 2026 — first published version.

9. Contact

Questions, requests, or reports: open an issue at github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/issues.

```python
html, n_cdn = re.subn(

The optional comment group `(?:<!--[\s\S]*?-->\s*)?` — non-greedy `[\s\S]*?` between `<!--` and `-->`: for a doc comment immediately preceding the tag, matches ✓. But danger: if an UNRELATED comment appears 100 lines earlier (e.g. the header comment at the top of the file), could the regex match from that earlier `<!--` all the way to the script tag, deleting everything in between? `[\s\S]*?` is non-greedy, so starting from the EARLIEST `<!--` that can still complete the pattern, the engine finds leftmost-longest... Regex scanning starts at leftmost position where a match is possible: at the FIRST `<!--` in the document (e.g. the big head comment at top). From there, `[\s\S]*?-->` tries to find the nearest `-->`. If the head comment closes with `-->`, then the optional group could complete there and then requires `<script type="module" src="inline_script_4.js">` IMMEDIATELY (no \s* between `-->` and `<script`... wait, the group includes `\s*` after `-->`). So the pattern is: `<!-- ...content... --> \s* <script...>`. The group is optional — if the nearest `-->` after an opening `<!--` is followed by \s* then the script tag, the whole span INCLUDING everything between the comment START and the script tag gets deleted? NO — wait: the group is `(?:<!--[\s\S]*?-->\s*)?` — the `[\s\S]*?` is bounded by the FIRST `-->` after `<!--`. So the comment group matches exactly one comment `<!--...-->` + trailing whitespace, then the script tag must follow. It deletes the comment + the tag. It can't span from an early comment through other content because `[\s\S]*?` stops at the first `-->`.

Hmm — BUT: leftmost-first matching: re.subn scans positions left to right; at each position tries to match. At position of first `<!--` (say the head doctype comment), `<!--` matches, `[\s\S]*?-->` matches to its closing `-->`, `\s*` eats whitespace, then requires `<script type="module" src="inline_script_4.js">` — if the next non-ws chars aren't that tag, the group backtracks: `[\s\S]*?` extends to the NEXT `-->`, and again after `\s*` requires the script tag... so it tries subsequent `-->`s until one is followed (after whitespace) by the inline_script_4 tag. If an earlier comment is followed later by lots of content and eventually the script tag — the whole span gets deleted! When could a `-->` be immediately followed by only whitespace up to the script tag? Only if the comment directly precedes the tag (normal case). Because after any `-->`, the next non-whitespace must be exactly `<script type="module" src="inline_script_4.js">`. In real index.html, each CDN tag has its own doc comment right above ✓ intended behavior. Could an UNRELATED comment directly precede inline_script_4's tag? In flutter_app/web/index.html — the tags each have their descriptive comments ✓. But e.g. if a comment sits right above inline_script_4's tag that ALSO describes something else — deletion of that comment is still fine.

Edge: a TWO-consecutive-comments block before a tag (comment A then comment B then tag): at position A: `<!--[\s\S]*?-->` → closes A; `\s*` then requires script — but B starts → backtrack: `[\s\S]*?` extends through B's end → deletes A+B+tag ✓ good.

# --- Optional fa web app (flutter_app → browser_ext/app). Build artifact. ---
if [ "$with_app" -eq 1 ]; then
  if ! command -v flutter >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "ERROR: --with-app passed but flutter is not installed — cannot build browser_ext/app/" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "building fa web app (flutter build web --release)…"
  # gh-1265 AC2: resolve against the committed lockfile — in the
  # build-macos release job this script's pub get is the ONLY
  # flutter_app resolution, so a plain resolve would float a
  # pubspec/lockfile skew into a green release build.
  # --base-href MUST match the panel-relative location: panel.js resolves
  # 'app/index.html' against panel/panel.html, so the bundle lives at
  # browser_ext/panel/app/ (a root-level copy is invisible to the panel).
  ( cd flutter_app && flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile >/dev/null
    # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (pubspec.yaml),
    # so the web build dies bundling it when the file is absent (#140).
    # Create it AFTER pub get — pub get removes a placeholder touched
    # earlier (runs 34593431895, 34596707238) — and keep it non-empty:
    # the populated placeholder is the shape build-macos.yml's app job
    # has shipped green. A real local .env (developer keys) is never
    # overwritten.
    if [ ! -f .env ]; then
      printf 'OPENROUTER_API_KEY=\nMODEL_ID=\nBASE_URL=\n' > .env
    fi
    FLUTTER_WEB_CANVASKIT_URL=./canvaskit/ \
    flutter build web --release --pwa-strategy=none --base-href=/panel/app/ \
      --dart-define=FA_HOST=extension )
  rm -rf browser_ext/panel/app
  mkdir -p browser_ext/panel/app
  cp -R flutter_app/build/web/. browser_ext/panel/app/
  # Shared prune (scripts/prune_flutter_assets.sh — same rulebook as every
  # packaging surface): assets/wasm is mobile-only (WasiSandboxShell via
  # env_factory_io.dart; the panel compiles env_factory_stub and runs
  # python/js/sqlite from cdn.jsdelivr.net, live interpreter = vendored
  # pyodide in offscreen/), plus the pub package's test fixtures
  # (coach_anny.glb, 5.6 MB) — dead weight here.
  bash scripts/prune_flutter_assets.sh browser_ext/panel/app/assets \
    assets/wasm packages/js_widget_runtime/test
  # CWS single-manifest rule (#291): the Flutter web build ships a PWA
  # manifest (panel/app/manifest.json, <link rel=manifest> in its
  # index.html) — the Chrome Web Store hard-rejects any package with more
  # than one manifest.json, and inside an extension page the PWA manifest
  # is functionally dead (extension pages are not installable PWAs). The
  # STAGED copy is DELETED-and-delinked, not renamed: nothing in the
  # extension consumes it, so an app.webmanifest rename would only ship
  # dead weight and keep a dead link. Sources stay untouched — this dir
  # is a gitignored build artifact re-copied from flutter_app/build/web
  # on every --with-app run; the unpacked dev flow (AC5) loads the same
  # stripped tree and boots identically (the panel never reads the PWA
  # manifest). Idempotent: a Flutter template without the link tag is a
  # no-op (#291 E3).
  python3 scripts/ext_package_guard.py strip browser_ext/panel/app
  # The extension CSP forbids remote hosts: point the bootstrap at the
  # bundled canvaskit copy (FLUTTER_WEB_CANVASKIT_URL does not reach the
  # generated bootstrap in this flutter).
  python3 - <<'PYS'
import glob
for f in glob.glob('flutter_app/build/web/flutter_bootstrap.js') + glob.glob('browser_ext/panel/app/flutter_bootstrap.js'):
    t = open(f).read()
    t = t.replace('https://www.gstatic.com/flutter-canvaskit/', './canvaskit/')
    t = t.replace('https:\\/\\/www.gstatic.com\\/flutter-canvaskit\\/', '.\\/canvaskit\\/')
    t = t.replace('"https://www.gstatic.com/flutter-canvaskit"', '"./canvaskit"')
    open(f, 'w').write(t)
PYS
  # The engine requests canvaskit under <engineRevision>/chromium/; the
  # build lays the copies flat — mirror the layout the bootstrap asks for.
  # Extract the FULL engine revision from the bootstrap config — a bounded
  # grep like [a-f0-9]{32} silently truncates the 40-char SHA1 and the
  # engine then 404s on canvaskit/<rev>/chromium/ (regression).
  REV=$(grep -o '"engineRevision":"[a-f0-9]*"' flutter_app/build/web/flutter_bootstrap.js | head -1 | sed 's/.*":"//;s/"//')
  if [ -n "$REV" ]; then
    if [ ${#REV} -ne 40 ]; then
      echo "FATAL: engineRevision '$REV' is not 40 hex chars" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    # Copy from the BUILD OUTPUT, never from the bundle copy itself —
    # the rev dir lives inside the bundle copy, so self-copying there
    # recurses into itself (File name too long on the next run).
    mkdir -p "browser_ext/panel/app/canvaskit/$REV"
    cp -R "flutter_app/build/web/canvaskit/." "browser_ext/panel/app/canvaskit/$REV/"

    for f in canvaskit.js canvaskit.wasm; do
      [ -f "browser_ext/panel/app/canvaskit/$REV/chromium/$f" ] || {
        echo "FATAL: canvaskit/$REV/chromium/$f missing after mirror" >&2
        exit 1
      }
    done
    echo "canvaskit mirrored to canvaskit/$REV/chromium/ (verified)"
    # canvaskit dedup (#1096 AC2): the engine only ever requests
    # canvaskit/<rev>/chromium/... (FLUTTER_WEB_CANVASKIT_URL=./canvaskit/
    # + the engineRevision the bootstrap pins), so the flat top-level
    # copy from build/web — canvaskit.js/wasm, chromium/, webparagraph/ —
    # is unreachable dead weight (~13MB duplicate subtree). Keep the rev
    # mirror (the verified-complete copy), drop its flat siblings.
    find browser_ext/panel/app/canvaskit -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 ! -name "$REV" -exec rm -rf {} +
    echo "canvaskit deduplicated to canvaskit/$REV/ (#1096)"
  else
    echo "FATAL: engineRevision not found in flutter_bootstrap.js" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  # The extension package must carry NO remote code (gh-1630 Blue Argon)
  # and its CSP forbids remote scripts: stage the on-device engine loaders
  # (WebLLM / transformers.js / LiteRT-LM) onto the package-local vendor
  # dir instead of the CDN imports the web build uses. Standalone,
  # idempotent script (test/browser_ext/cws_compliance_test.dart exercises
  # it) — replaces the pre-gh-1630 ondevice_stub.js failure shim: the
  # engines are vendored now, so they LOAD instead of degrading.
  python3 scripts/stage_extension_panel.py --app-dir browser_ext/panel/app
  echo "bundled fa web app (browser_ext/panel/app/)"
fi

# A staged app from an earlier --with-app run can outlive the flag (the
# dir is gitignored and never cleaned): without this, a plain local build
# zips panel/app/manifest.json verbatim and the guard fails the package
# (CWS single-manifest rule, #291). Strip unconditionally — idempotent.
if [ -d browser_ext/panel/app ]; then
  if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    python3 scripts/ext_package_guard.py strip browser_ext/panel/app
  else
    echo "WARNING: no python3 — cannot strip browser_ext/panel/app;" \
         "the packaging guard below hard-requires python3 anyway" >&2
  fi
fi

mkdir -p build
rm -f build/fa-extension.zip

# CWS-strict manifest (owner report 2026-10-11): the store uploader
# rejects // comments ("manifest.json:17:2: missing value") AND the dev
# "key" field ("key field is not allowed in manifest" — CWS owns the
# key, the source pins it only for a stable local dev id). The zip must
# carry a comment-stripped, key-less manifest while the source keeps
# both. Staged under build/pack/ so the zip entry name stays exactly
# "manifest.json". The ext_package_guard check below re-parses the
# packaged manifest STRICTLY and rejects "key", so a regression here
# fails the build, never the store upload.
mkdir -p build/pack
if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  python3 -c '
import json, re, sys
raw = open(sys.argv[1]).read()
m = json.loads(re.sub(r"^\s*//.*$", "", raw, flags=re.M))
m.pop("key", None)
open(sys.argv[2], "w").write(json.dumps(m, indent=2) + "\n")
' "$manifest" build/pack/manifest.json
elif command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  node -e 'const fs=require("fs"); const m=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(process.argv[1], "utf8").replace(/^\s*\/\/.*$/gm, "")); delete m.key; fs.writeFileSync(process.argv[2], JSON.stringify(m, null, 2) + "\n")' "$manifest" build/pack/manifest.json
else
  echo "WARNING: no python3/node — packaging the RAW source manifest;" \
       "the strict guard below is expected to fail (CWS needs stripped JSON)" >&2
  cp "$manifest" build/pack/manifest.json
fi

if command -v zip >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  runtime="sw content panel icons offscreen.html offscreen vendor"
  # panel/app rides inside the panel/ dir — no separate root entry.
  # The stripped CWS manifest rides from build/pack/ (the verbatim source
  # manifest.json stays out of the zip on purpose).
  ( cd browser_ext && zip -qr ../build/fa-extension.zip $runtime \
      -x 'sw/agent.js.map' 'sw/agent.js.deps' )
  ( cd build/pack && zip -q ../fa-extension.zip manifest.json )
else
python3 - <<'PY'
import os, zipfile
RUNTIME_DIRS = ("sw", "content", "panel", "icons", "offscreen", "vendor")
SKIP_NAMES = {"README.md", "agent.js.map", "agent.js.deps"}
with zipfile.ZipFile("build/fa-extension.zip", "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as z:
    # build/pack/manifest.json is the comment-stripped CWS copy made above.
    z.write("build/pack/manifest.json", "manifest.json")
    z.write("browser_ext/offscreen.html", "offscreen.html")
    for d in RUNTIME_DIRS:

Fa (Flutter Agent Harness) · Effective date: October 15, 2026
English Русский

English

This policy covers the Fa applications — the mobile/desktop/web app and the Fa browser extension ("fa — browser agent") — built on the open-source Flutter Agent Harness. The short version: the products are designed local-first — your keys, chats, and files stay on your device, and content leaves the device only to the AI providers you explicitly connect.

1. Data we collect

Fa has no accounts and no sign-up. Depending on how you use it, the following data is handled by the app on your device:

  • Chat and conversation content you send through fa — your prompts, the agent's replies, and the conversation context.
  • Provider API keys you enter so fa can talk to your chosen AI provider (e.g. OpenRouter, Anthropic, or a custom endpoint).
  • Page content the agent reads when you ask it to act on a page (text, screenshots, cookies needed for the flow you drive, history/bookmark entries you explicitly reference).
  • Local files you attach or files the agent creates for you in its sandbox.
  • The developer receives none of the above. There is no telemetry or analytics in the browser extension at all; in the mobile/desktop app, optional Firebase analytics/crash reporting is described in section 2 and never includes message text, keys, or file contents.

2. How we handle data

  • On-device processing. Prompts, tool results, and files are processed on your device. Nothing is proxied through the developer: fa operates no servers that receive your conversation content, keys, or files.
  • AI requests. When you chat with the agent, the relevant prompt and context are sent — directly from your device — to the AI providers you configure (your keys, your base URLs). Those providers process your data under their own privacy policies.
  • Analytics (app only). Where the platform makes it available, the mobile/desktop app sends Firebase Analytics events with metadata only (event names, provider/model identifiers, coarse buckets) and Firebase Crashlytics crash reports (stack traces, device model, OS version) — never API keys, message text, prompts, or file contents. The browser extension sends no analytics and no crash reports.
  • Website analytics. The landing page (fa1.dev) uses Google Analytics 4 with IP anonymization to count page views and outbound clicks. It sets no advertising cookies and tracks nothing inside the app you run from the page.

3. Data storage

  • Everything fa keeps — chats, sessions, settings, provider keys, sandbox files — is stored locally on your device or in your browser: the platform Keychain / secure store for keys (app), chrome.storage and extension storage for extension state, OPFS/IndexedDB for web sandboxes and downloaded model caches.
  • Nothing is stored cloud-side by the extension or the developer. There is no fa account and no fa cloud.
  • On-device model files you choose to download (e.g. small LLM weights) are stored in your browser's storage and are never uploaded.

4. Data sharing

  • We do not sell your data, and we do not share it with third parties for marketing.
  • The only third parties that receive your content are the model providers you explicitly configure (your requests go directly to their endpoints).
  • Native messaging. When you pair the extension with a local fa CLI helper, the extension and that local helper exchange messages between themselves on your machine — this traffic does not involve the developer or any server.
  • Optional system permissions (notifications, microphone, calendar, contacts, health, home) are requested only in context for features you invoke, and the data they touch is processed on-device only.

5. Retention & deletion

  • Local data persists until you delete it: clear a chat/session inside the app, clear the extension's data via browser settings, or uninstall — uninstalling the app or extension removes its locally stored data.
  • Downloaded model weights and web-sandbox files live in your browser storage and can be cleared the same way (site data / extension data).
  • Firebase analytics/crash data (app only), where enabled, is retained per Google's standard Firebase retention and contains no message content.

6. Security

  • Keys. Provider API keys are stored in the platform Keychain (iOS/macOS) or the local secure store / browser storage of the app sandbox, and are transmitted only to the provider they belong to.
  • Redaction. A layered secret-redaction pipeline masks credentials and token-shaped strings in logs, session files, and tool output before they are persisted, so secrets do not leak into recorded sessions.
  • Approvals. Sensitive agent actions (running commands, opening pages, sending data out of the browser) pass an approval gate you control, from ask-per-action to fully unattended modes.
  • The extension loads all interpreter/LLM engine code from inside the package (no remotely hosted code), and its permissions are limited to what its features call.

7. Children's privacy

The app and the extension are not directed at children under 13 (or the equivalent minimum age in your jurisdiction), and we do not knowingly collect personal data from them.

8. Changes to this policy

Changes are posted at this URL with a new effective date.

  • October 15, 2026 — restructured into the nine Chrome Web Store mandatory sections; added the browser extension (local engine code, native messaging, no telemetry).
  • July 29, 2026 — first published version.

9. Contact

Questions, requests, or reports: open an issue at github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/issues.

The new comment says "any vendored-asset load failure is exactly what this checker exists to catch", but the filter one line down still exempts every error containing `is not defined`:

final fatal = errors.where((e) => !e.contains('is not defined'));

That is the signature failure of a vendored loader that did not install its global: if `vendor_loader_webllm.js` / `vendor_loader_transformers.js` fails before assigning `window.webllm` / `window.transformersjs` (or `m.Engine` comes back undefined for LiteRT), the Dart side's first touch logs `… is not defined` — silently downgraded to non-fatal. The PR's AC2 evidence for the three panel engines is only "panel renders + console fatal=0", so a silently degraded engine family would still pass this gate.

Note `litertLmReady` rejections are caught by design (the Dart side awaits and degrades), so a failed local import can be console-silent end-to-end.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the "re-fetching" path never re-fetches**

When a file exists in the vendor tree but its sha256 drifts from the lock (full mode), this line prints "re-fetching" — but control falls through to `verify(data)` on the **already-on-disk drifted bytes**, which can only fail the checksum and abort the build. # --- Optional fa web app (flutter_app → browser_ext/app). Build artifact. ---
if [ "$with_app" -eq 1 ]; then
  if ! command -v flutter >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "ERROR: --with-app passed but flutter is not installed — cannot build browser_ext/app/" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "building fa web app (flutter build web --release)…"
  # gh-1265 AC2: resolve against the committed lockfile — in the
  # build-macos release job this script's pub get is the ONLY
  # flutter_app resolution, so a plain resolve would float a
  # pubspec/lockfile skew into a green release build.
  # --base-href MUST match the panel-relative location: panel.js resolves
  # 'app/index.html' against panel/panel.html, so the bundle lives at
  # browser_ext/panel/app/ (a root-level copy is invisible to the panel).
  ( cd flutter_app && flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile >/dev/null
    # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (pubspec.yaml),
    # so the web build dies bundling it when the file is absent (#140).
    # Create it AFTER pub get — pub get removes a placeholder touched
    # earlier (runs 34593431895, 34596707238) — and keep it non-empty:
    # the populated placeholder is the shape build-macos.yml's app job
    # has shipped green. A real local .env (developer keys) is never
    # overwritten.
    if [ ! -f .env ]; then
      printf 'OPENROUTER_API_KEY=\nMODEL_ID=\nBASE_URL=\n' > .env
    fi
    FLUTTER_WEB_CANVASKIT_URL=./canvaskit/ \
    flutter build web --release --pwa-strategy=none --base-href=/panel/app/ \
      --dart-define=FA_HOST=extension )
  rm -rf browser_ext/panel/app
  mkdir -p browser_ext/panel/app
  cp -R flutter_app/build/web/. browser_ext/panel/app/
  # Shared prune (scripts/prune_flutter_assets.sh — same rulebook as every
  # packaging surface): assets/wasm is mobile-only (WasiSandboxShell via
  # env_factory_io.dart; the panel compiles env_factory_stub and runs
  # python/js/sqlite from cdn.jsdelivr.net, live interpreter = vendored
  # pyodide in offscreen/), plus the pub package's test fixtures
  # (coach_anny.glb, 5.6 MB) — dead weight here.
  bash scripts/prune_flutter_assets.sh browser_ext/panel/app/assets \
    assets/wasm packages/js_widget_runtime/test
  # CWS single-manifest rule (#291): the Flutter web build ships a PWA
  # manifest (panel/app/manifest.json, <link rel=manifest> in its
  # index.html) — the Chrome Web Store hard-rejects any package with more
  # than one manifest.json, and inside an extension page the PWA manifest
  # is functionally dead (extension pages are not installable PWAs). The
  # STAGED copy is DELETED-and-delinked, not renamed: nothing in the
  # extension consumes it, so an app.webmanifest rename would only ship
  # dead weight and keep a dead link. Sources stay untouched — this dir
  # is a gitignored build artifact re-copied from flutter_app/build/web
  # on every --with-app run; the unpacked dev flow (AC5) loads the same
  # stripped tree and boots identically (the panel never reads the PWA
  # manifest). Idempotent: a Flutter template without the link tag is a
  # no-op (#291 E3).
  python3 scripts/ext_package_guard.py strip browser_ext/panel/app
  # The extension CSP forbids remote hosts: point the bootstrap at the
  # bundled canvaskit copy (FLUTTER_WEB_CANVASKIT_URL does not reach the
  # generated bootstrap in this flutter).
  python3 - <<'PYS'
import glob
for f in glob.glob('flutter_app/build/web/flutter_bootstrap.js') + glob.glob('browser_ext/panel/app/flutter_bootstrap.js'):
    t = open(f).read()
    t = t.replace('https://www.gstatic.com/flutter-canvaskit/', './canvaskit/')
    t = t.replace('https:\\/\\/www.gstatic.com\\/flutter-canvaskit\\/', '.\\/canvaskit\\/')
    t = t.replace('"https://www.gstatic.com/flutter-canvaskit"', '"./canvaskit"')
    open(f, 'w').write(t)
PYS
  # The engine requests canvaskit under <engineRevision>/chromium/; the
  # build lays the copies flat — mirror the layout the bootstrap asks for.
  # Extract the FULL engine revision from the bootstrap config — a bounded
  # grep like [a-f0-9]{32} silently truncates the 40-char SHA1 and the
  # engine then 404s on canvaskit/<rev>/chromium/ (regression).
  REV=$(grep -o '"engineRevision":"[a-f0-9]*"' flutter_app/build/web/flutter_bootstrap.js | head -1 | sed 's/.*":"//;s/"//')
  if [ -n "$REV" ]; then
    if [ ${#REV} -ne 40 ]; then
      echo "FATAL: engineRevision '$REV' is not 40 hex chars" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    # Copy from the BUILD OUTPUT, never from the bundle copy itself —
    # the rev dir lives inside the bundle copy, so self-copying there
    # recurses into itself (File name too long on the next run).
    mkdir -p "browser_ext/panel/app/canvaskit/$REV"
    cp -R "flutter_app/build/web/canvaskit/." "browser_ext/panel/app/canvaskit/$REV/"

      }
    done
    echo "canvaskit mirrored to canvaskit/$REV/chromium/ (verified)"
    # canvaskit dedup (#1096 AC2): the engine only ever requests
    # canvaskit/<rev>/chromium/... (FLUTTER_WEB_CANVASKIT_URL=./canvaskit/
    # + the engineRevision the bootstrap pins), so the flat top-level
    # copy from build/web — canvaskit.js/wasm, chromium/, webparagraph/ —
    # is unreachable dead weight (~13MB duplicate subtree). Keep the rev
    # mirror (the verified-complete copy), drop its flat siblings.
    find browser_ext/panel/app/canvaskit -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 ! -name "$REV" -exec rm -rf {} +
    echo "canvaskit deduplicated to canvaskit/$REV/ (#1096)"
  else
    echo "FATAL: engineRevision not found in flutter_bootstrap.js" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  # The extension package must carry NO remote code (gh-1630 Blue Argon)
  # and its CSP forbids remote scripts: stage the on-device engine loaders
  # (WebLLM / transformers.js / LiteRT-LM) onto the package-local vendor
  # dir instead of the CDN imports the web build uses. Standalone,
  # idempotent script (test/browser_ext/cws_compliance_test.dart exercises
  # it) — replaces the pre-gh-1630 ondevice_stub.js failure shim: the
  # engines are vendored now, so they LOAD instead of degrading.
  python3 scripts/stage_extension_panel.py --app-dir browser_ext/panel/app
  echo "bundled fa web app (browser_ext/panel/app/)"
fi

# A staged app from an earlier --with-app run can outlive the flag (the
# dir is gitignored and never cleaned): without this, a plain local build
# zips panel/app/manifest.json verbatim and the guard fails the package
# (CWS single-manifest rule, #291). Strip unconditionally — idempotent.
if [ -d browser_ext/panel/app ]; then
  if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    python3 scripts/ext_package_guard.py strip browser_ext/panel/app
  else
    echo "WARNING: no python3 — cannot strip browser_ext/panel/app;" \
         "the packaging guard below hard-requires python3 anyway" >&2
  fi
fi

mkdir -p build
rm -f build/fa-extension.zip

# CWS-strict manifest (owner report 2026-10-11): the store uploader
# rejects // comments ("manifest.json:17:2: missing value") AND the dev
# "key" field ("key field is not allowed in manifest" — CWS owns the
# key, the source pins it only for a stable local dev id). The zip must
# carry a comment-stripped, key-less manifest while the source keeps
# both. Staged under build/pack/ so the zip entry name stays exactly
# "manifest.json". The ext_package_guard check below re-parses the
# packaged manifest STRICTLY and rejects "key", so a regression here
# fails the build, never the store upload.
mkdir -p build/pack
if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  python3 -c '
import json, re, sys
raw = open(sys.argv[1]).read()
m = json.loads(re.sub(r"^\s*//.*$", "", raw, flags=re.M))
m.pop("key", None)
open(sys.argv[2], "w").write(json.dumps(m, indent=2) + "\n")
' "$manifest" build/pack/manifest.json
elif command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  node -e 'const fs=require("fs"); const m=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(process.argv[1], "utf8").replace(/^\s*\/\/.*$/gm, "")); delete m.key; fs.writeFileSync(process.argv[2], JSON.stringify(m, null, 2) + "\n")' "$manifest" build/pack/manifest.json
else
  echo "WARNING: no python3/node — packaging the RAW source manifest;" \
       "the strict guard below is expected to fail (CWS needs stripped JSON)" >&2
  cp "$manifest" build/pack/manifest.json
fi

if command -v zip >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  runtime="sw content panel icons offscreen.html offscreen vendor"
  # panel/app rides inside the panel/ dir — no separate root entry.
  # The stripped CWS manifest rides from build/pack/ (the verbatim source
  # manifest.json stays out of the zip on purpose).
  ( cd browser_ext && zip -qr ../build/fa-extension.zip $runtime \
      -x 'sw/agent.js.map' 'sw/agent.js.deps' )
  ( cd build/pack && zip -q ../fa-extension.zip manifest.json )
else
python3 - <<'PY'
import os, zipfile
RUNTIME_DIRS = ("sw", "content", "panel", "icons", "offscreen", "vendor")
SKIP_NAMES = {"README.md", "agent.js.map", "agent.js.deps"}
with zipfile.ZipFile("build/fa-extension.zip", "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as z:
    # build/pack/manifest.json is the comment-stripped CWS copy made above.
    z.write("build/pack/manifest.json", "manifest.json")
    z.write("browser_ext/offscreen.html", "offscreen.html")
    for d in RUNTIME_DIRS:

Fa (Flutter Agent Harness) · Effective date: October 15, 2026
English Русский

English

This policy covers the Fa applications — the mobile/desktop/web app and the Fa browser extension ("fa — browser agent") — built on the open-source Flutter Agent Harness. The short version: the products are designed local-first — your keys, chats, and files stay on your device, and content leaves the device only to the AI providers you explicitly connect.

1. Data we collect

Fa has no accounts and no sign-up. Depending on how you use it, the following data is handled by the app on your device:

  • Chat and conversation content you send through fa — your prompts, the agent's replies, and the conversation context.
  • Provider API keys you enter so fa can talk to your chosen AI provider (e.g. OpenRouter, Anthropic, or a custom endpoint).
  • Page content the agent reads when you ask it to act on a page (text, screenshots, cookies needed for the flow you drive, history/bookmark entries you explicitly reference).
  • Local files you attach or files the agent creates for you in its sandbox.
  • The developer receives none of the above. There is no telemetry or analytics in the browser extension at all; in the mobile/desktop app, optional Firebase analytics/crash reporting is described in section 2 and never includes message text, keys, or file contents.

2. How we handle data

  • On-device processing. Prompts, tool results, and files are processed on your device. Nothing is proxied through the developer: fa operates no servers that receive your conversation content, keys, or files.
  • AI requests. When you chat with the agent, the relevant prompt and context are sent — directly from your device — to the AI providers you configure (your keys, your base URLs). Those providers process your data under their own privacy policies.
  • Analytics (app only). Where the platform makes it available, the mobile/desktop app sends Firebase Analytics events with metadata only (event names, provider/model identifiers, coarse buckets) and Firebase Crashlytics crash reports (stack traces, device model, OS version) — never API keys, message text, prompts, or file contents. The browser extension sends no analytics and no crash reports.
  • Website analytics. The landing page (fa1.dev) uses Google Analytics 4 with IP anonymization to count page views and outbound clicks. It sets no advertising cookies and tracks nothing inside the app you run from the page.

3. Data storage

  • Everything fa keeps — chats, sessions, settings, provider keys, sandbox files — is stored locally on your device or in your browser: the platform Keychain / secure store for keys (app), chrome.storage and extension storage for extension state, OPFS/IndexedDB for web sandboxes and downloaded model caches.
  • Nothing is stored cloud-side by the extension or the developer. There is no fa account and no fa cloud.
  • On-device model files you choose to download (e.g. small LLM weights) are stored in your browser's storage and are never uploaded.

4. Data sharing

  • We do not sell your data, and we do not share it with third parties for marketing.
  • The only third parties that receive your content are the model providers you explicitly configure (your requests go directly to their endpoints).
  • Native messaging. When you pair the extension with a local fa CLI helper, the extension and that local helper exchange messages between themselves on your machine — this traffic does not involve the developer or any server.
  • Optional system permissions (notifications, microphone, calendar, contacts, health, home) are requested only in context for features you invoke, and the data they touch is processed on-device only.

5. Retention & deletion

  • Local data persists until you delete it: clear a chat/session inside the app, clear the extension's data via browser settings, or uninstall — uninstalling the app or extension removes its locally stored data.
  • Downloaded model weights and web-sandbox files live in your browser storage and can be cleared the same way (site data / extension data).
  • Firebase analytics/crash data (app only), where enabled, is retained per Google's standard Firebase retention and contains no message content.

6. Security

  • Keys. Provider API keys are stored in the platform Keychain (iOS/macOS) or the local secure store / browser storage of the app sandbox, and are transmitted only to the provider they belong to.
  • Redaction. A layered secret-redaction pipeline masks credentials and token-shaped strings in logs, session files, and tool output before they are persisted, so secrets do not leak into recorded sessions.
  • Approvals. Sensitive agent actions (running commands, opening pages, sending data out of the browser) pass an approval gate you control, from ask-per-action to fully unattended modes.
  • The extension loads all interpreter/LLM engine code from inside the package (no remotely hosted code), and its permissions are limited to what its features call.

7. Children's privacy

The app and the extension are not directed at children under 13 (or the equivalent minimum age in your jurisdiction), and we do not knowingly collect personal data from them.

8. Changes to this policy

Changes are posted at this URL with a new effective date.

  • October 15, 2026 — restructured into the nine Chrome Web Store mandatory sections; added the browser extension (local engine code, native messaging, no telemetry).
  • July 29, 2026 — first published version.

9. Contact

The new comment says "any vendored-asset load failure is exactly what this checker exists to catch", but the filter one line down still exempts every error containing `is not defined`:

```dart
final fatal = errors.where((e) => !e.contains('is not defined'));

That is the signature failure of a vendored loader that did not install its global: if `vendor_loader_webllm.js` / `vendor_loader_transformers.js` fails before assigning `window.webllm` / `window.transformersjs` (or `m.Engine` comes back undefined for LiteRT), the Dart side's first touch logs `… is not defined` — silently downgraded to non-fatal. The PR's AC2 evidence for the three panel engines is only "panel renders + console fatal=0", so a silently degraded engine family would still pass this gate.

Note `litertLmReady` rejections are caught by design (the Dart side awaits and degrades), so a failed local import can be console-silent end-to-end.

Suggestions:
- assert the constructs explicitly: extend the panel probe/e2e to check `!!window.webllm`, `!!window.transformersjs`, and that `window.litertLmReady` settles fulfilled (all three are vendored and must load — that is the whole point of gh-1630), or

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the "re-fetching" path never re-fetches**

- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1631

## PR Description

Closes #1630
### Root Cause

The extension shipped remotely-hosted code: the panel app bundled the web
build's jsdelivr imports (on-device engines + the interpreters' CDN
constants in `main.dart.js`), and the offscreen runtimes rode unpinned
floating URLs with no re-verification. The manifest also declared five
permissions with zero call sites (`contentSettings`, `downloads`,
`fontSettings`, `identity`, `desktopCapture`) and a CSP without
`'wasm-unsafe-eval'`, and `site/privacy.html` missed six mandatory sections
in EN/RU — four independent rejection grounds, none addressed before
this fix.

### Previous Attempt

The previous dev leg (run 38722657674) failed without landing a fix — its
auto-save WIP commits net out to no diff vs main. Every rejection ground
was still open when this leg started.

### Fix

- `browser_ext/vendor.lock.json` + `scripts/fetch_vendor_assets.sh`: all six
  engines (quickjs, pyodide, sqljs, webllm, transformers, litert) pinned
  per-artifact with sha256 + version-pinned URLs; rewrites the bundled
  remote constants onto package-local dirs, re-verifies the tree on every
  build, generates the quickjs ffi-types shim.
- `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/web_interpreters_urls.dart` (new): the
  interpreters resolve per build via `--dart-define=FA_HOST=extension` —
  the extension compiles only `../../vendor/interpreters/...` paths; the
  CDN constants are tree-shaken out (verified on the compiled artifact:
  0 jsdelivr markers in `main.dart.js`). Pyodide now gets an explicit
  `indexURL` in both builds (no silent remote fallback).
- `scripts/stage_extension_panel.py` (new): replaces the panel's three CDN
  engine-loader tags (and their comments/orphaned modules) with
  `vendor_loader_*.js` importing from the package-local vendor dir — the
  on-device engines WORK in the extension now (the old stub disabled them).
- `browser_ext/manifest.json`: dead permissions removed; CSP is
  `'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'`.
- `site/privacy.html` + `PRIVACY.md`: nine mandatory sections (`data-sec`
  anchored) in EN and RU; store listing links the live URL.
- `scripts/check_cws_compliance.py` (new) + `ext_package_guard.py` remote
  scan: AC1 byte-scan of sources AND the built zip, manifest/privacy/lock
  asserts — wired into `.github/workflows/browser-ext.yml`, red blocks
  merge (REG-1).

### Test Coverage

- `test/browser_ext/cws_compliance_test.dart` (8), `test/site/privacy_policy_test.dart` (4),
  `flutter_app/test/web_interpreters_urls_test.dart` (3) — new; the
  compliance tests failed before the fix, pass after.
- Full suites: root dart 10,982 passed / 0 failed; browser_ext/dart 451;
  node 46; Playwright run-script (vendored quickjs + pyodide in the real
  extension) 6/6; panel-app e2e 2 passed (real app renders, no fatal
  overlay).
- Artifact: `build/fa-extension.zip` (155 entries) passes the packaging
  guard — byte-scan finds zero remote-code markers in the package;
  compiled `main.dart.js`: 0 jsdelivr, 5 `vendor/interpreters` paths.
- Panel console checker (jsdelivr allowlist removed — any CDN mention is
  now fatal): `fatal=0 consoleErrors=0` in real headless Chrome.

### Notes

- The extension's CSP keeps blocking every remote host; `'wasm-unsafe-eval'`
  is the Google-recommended scoped exception the vendored wasm engines
  need (pyodide/onnxruntime/quickjs) — it does not re-enable `eval`.
- The hosted web app and Office taskpane keep loading engines from CDNs
  (unchanged behavior, tree-shaken out of the extension build).

# --- Optional fa web app (flutter_app → browser_ext/app). Build artifact. ---
if [ "$with_app" -eq 1 ]; then
  if ! command -v flutter >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "ERROR: --with-app passed but flutter is not installed — cannot build browser_ext/app/" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "building fa web app (flutter build web --release)…"
  # gh-1265 AC2: resolve against the committed lockfile — in the
  # build-macos release job this script's pub get is the ONLY
  # flutter_app resolution, so a plain resolve would float a
  # pubspec/lockfile skew into a green release build.
  # --base-href MUST match the panel-relative location: panel.js resolves
  # 'app/index.html' against panel/panel.html, so the bundle lives at
  # browser_ext/panel/app/ (a root-level copy is invisible to the panel).
  ( cd flutter_app && flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile >/dev/null
    # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (pubspec.yaml),
    # so the web build dies bundling it when the file is absent (#140).
    # Create it AFTER pub get — pub get removes a placeholder touched
    # earlier (runs 34593431895, 34596707238) — and keep it non-empty:
    # the populated placeholder is the shape build-macos.yml's app job
    # has shipped green. A real local .env (developer keys) is never
    # overwritten.
    if [ ! -f .env ]; then
      printf 'OPENROUTER_API_KEY=\nMODEL_ID=\nBASE_URL=\n' > .env
    fi
    FLUTTER_WEB_CANVASKIT_URL=./canvaskit/ \
    flutter build web --release --pwa-strategy=none --base-href=/panel/app/ \
      --dart-define=FA_HOST=extension )
  rm -rf browser_ext/panel/app
  mkdir -p browser_ext/panel/app
  cp -R flutter_app/build/web/. browser_ext/panel/app/
  # Shared prune (scripts/prune_flutter_assets.sh — same rulebook as every
  # packaging surface): assets/wasm is mobile-only (WasiSandboxShell via
  # env_factory_io.dart; the panel compiles env_factory_stub and runs
  # python/js/sqlite from cdn.jsdelivr.net, live interpreter = vendored
  # pyodide in offscreen/), plus the pub package's test fixtures
  # (coach_anny.glb, 5.6 MB) — dead weight here.
  bash scripts/prune_flutter_assets.sh browser_ext/panel/app/assets \
    assets/wasm packages/js_widget_runtime/test
  # CWS single-manifest rule (#291): the Flutter web build ships a PWA
  # manifest (panel/app/manifest.json, <link rel=manifest> in its
  # index.html) — the Chrome Web Store hard-rejects any package with more
  # than one manifest.json, and inside an extension page the PWA manifest
  # is functionally dead (extension pages are not installable PWAs). The
  # STAGED copy is DELETED-and-delinked, not renamed: nothing in the
  # extension consumes it, so an app.webmanifest rename would only ship
  # dead weight and keep a dead link. Sources stay untouched — this dir
  # is a gitignored build artifact re-copied from flutter_app/build/web
  # on every --with-app run; the unpacked dev flow (AC5) loads the same
  # stripped tree and boots identically (the panel never reads the PWA
  # manifest). Idempotent: a Flutter template without the link tag is a
  # no-op (#291 E3).
  python3 scripts/ext_package_guard.py strip browser_ext/panel/app
  # The extension CSP forbids remote hosts: point the bootstrap at the
  # bundled canvaskit copy (FLUTTER_WEB_CANVASKIT_URL does not reach the
  # generated bootstrap in this flutter).
  python3 - <<'PYS'
import glob
for f in glob.glob('flutter_app/build/web/flutter_bootstrap.js') + glob.glob('browser_ext/panel/app/flutter_bootstrap.js'):
    t = open(f).read()
    t = t.replace('https://www.gstatic.com/flutter-canvaskit/', './canvaskit/')
    t = t.replace('https:\\/\\/www.gstatic.com\\/flutter-canvaskit\\/', '.\\/canvaskit\\/')
    t = t.replace('"https://www.gstatic.com/flutter-canvaskit"', '"./canvaskit"')
    open(f, 'w').write(t)
PYS
  # The engine requests canvaskit under <engineRevision>/chromium/; the
  # build lays the copies flat — mirror the layout the bootstrap asks for.
  # Extract the FULL engine revision from the bootstrap config — a bounded
  # grep like [a-f0-9]{32} silently truncates the 40-char SHA1 and the
  # engine then 404s on canvaskit/<rev>/chromium/ (regression).
  REV=$(grep -o '"engineRevision":"[a-f0-9]*"' flutter_app/build/web/flutter_bootstrap.js | head -1 | sed 's/.*":"//;s/"//')
  if [ -n "$REV" ]; then
    if [ ${#REV} -ne 40 ]; then
      echo "FATAL: engineRevision '$REV' is not 40 hex chars" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    # Copy from the BUILD OUTPUT, never from the bundle copy itself —
    # the rev dir lives inside the bundle copy, so self-copying there
    # recurses into itself (File name too long on the next run).
    mkdir -p "browser_ext/panel/app/canvaskit/$REV"
    cp -R "flutter_app/build/web/canvaskit/." "browser_ext/panel/app/canvaskit/$REV/"

cp -R "flutter_app/build/web/canvaskit/." "browser_ext/panel/app/canvaskit/$REV/"
    for f in canvaskit.js canvaskit.wasm; do
      [ -f "browser_ext/panel/app/canvaskit/$REV/chromium/$f" ] || {
        echo "FATAL: canvaskit/$REV/chromium/$f missing after mirror" >&2
        exit 1
      }
    done
    echo "canvaskit mirrored to canvaskit/$REV/chromium/ (verified)"
    # canvaskit dedup (#1096 AC2): the engine only ever requests
    # canvaskit/<rev>/chromium/... (FLUTTER_WEB_CANVASKIT_URL=./canvaskit/
    # + the engineRevision the bootstrap pins), so the flat top-level
    # copy from build/web — canvaskit.js/wasm, chromium/, webparagraph/ —
    # is unreachable dead weight (~13MB duplicate subtree). Keep the rev
    # mirror (the verified-complete copy), drop its flat siblings.
    find browser_ext/panel/app/canvaskit -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 ! -name "$REV" -exec rm -rf {} +
    echo "canvaskit deduplicated to canvaskit/$REV/ (#1096)"
  else
    echo "FATAL: engineRevision not found in flutter_bootstrap.js" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  # The extension package must carry NO remote code (gh-1630 Blue Argon)
  # and its CSP forbids remote scripts: stage the on-device engine loaders
  # (WebLLM / transformers.js / LiteRT-LM) onto the package-local vendor
  # dir instead of the CDN imports the web build uses. Standalone,
  # idempotent script (test/browser_ext/cws_compliance_test.dart exercises
  # it) — replaces the pre-gh-1630 ondevice_stub.js failure shim: the
  # engines are vendored now, so they LOAD instead of degrading.
  python3 scripts/stage_extension_panel.py --app-dir browser_ext/panel/app
  echo "bundled fa web app (browser_ext/panel/app/)"
fi

# A staged app from an earlier --with-app run can outlive the flag (the
# dir is gitignored and never cleaned): without this, a plain local build
# zips panel/app/manifest.json verbatim and the guard fails the package
# (CWS single-manifest rule, #291). Strip unconditionally — idempotent.
if [ -d browser_ext/panel/app ]; then
  if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    python3 scripts/ext_package_guard.py strip browser_ext/panel/app
  else
    echo "WARNING: no python3 — cannot strip browser_ext/panel/app;" \
         "the packaging guard below hard-requires python3 anyway" >&2
  fi
fi

mkdir -p build
rm -f build/fa-extension.zip

# CWS-strict manifest (owner report 2026-10-11): the store uploader
# rejects // comments ("manifest.json:17:2: missing value") AND the dev
# "key" field ("key field is not allowed in manifest" — CWS owns the
# key, the source pins it only for a stable local dev id). The zip must
# carry a comment-stripped, key-less manifest while the source keeps
# both. Staged under build/pack/ so the zip entry name stays exactly
# "manifest.json". The ext_package_guard check below re-parses the
# packaged manifest STRICTLY and rejects "key", so a regression here
# fails the build, never the store upload.
mkdir -p build/pack
if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  python3 -c '
import json, re, sys
raw = open(sys.argv[1]).read()
m = json.loads(re.sub(r"^\s*//.*$", "", raw, flags=re.M))
m.pop("key", None)
open(sys.argv[2], "w").write(json.dumps(m, indent=2) + "\n")
' "$manifest" build/pack/manifest.json
elif command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  node -e 'const fs=require("fs"); const m=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(process.argv[1], "utf8").replace(/^\s*\/\/.*$/gm, "")); delete m.key; fs.writeFileSync(process.argv[2], JSON.stringify(m, null, 2) + "\n")' "$manifest" build/pack/manifest.json
else
  echo "WARNING: no python3/node — packaging the RAW source manifest;" \
       "the strict guard below is expected to fail (CWS needs stripped JSON)" >&2
  cp "$manifest" build/pack/manifest.json
fi

if command -v zip >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  runtime="sw content panel icons offscreen.html offscreen vendor"
  # panel/app rides inside the panel/ dir — no separate root entry.
  # The stripped CWS manifest rides from build/pack/ (the verbatim source
  # manifest.json stays out of the zip on purpose).
  ( cd browser_ext && zip -qr ../build/fa-extension.zip $runtime \
      -x 'sw/agent.js.map' 'sw/agent.js.deps' )
  ( cd build/pack && zip -q ../fa-extension.zip manifest.json )
else
python3 - <<'PY'
import os, zipfile
RUNTIME_DIRS = ("sw", "content", "panel", "icons", "offscreen", "vendor")
SKIP_NAMES = {"README.md", "agent.js.map", "agent.js.deps"}
with zipfile.ZipFile("build/fa-extension.zip", "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as z:
    # build/pack/manifest.json is the comment-stripped CWS copy made above.
    z.write("build/pack/manifest.json", "manifest.json")
    z.write("browser_ext/offscreen.html", "offscreen.html")
    for d in RUNTIME_DIRS:

Fa (Flutter Agent Harness) · Effective date: October 15, 2026
English Русский

English

This policy covers the Fa applications — the mobile/desktop/web app and the Fa browser extension ("fa — browser agent") — built on the open-source Flutter Agent Harness. The short version: the products are designed local-first — your keys, chats, and files stay on your device, and content leaves the device only to the AI providers you explicitly connect.

1. Data we collect

Fa has no accounts and no sign-up. Depending on how you use it, the following data is handled by the app on your device:

  • Chat and conversation content you send through fa — your prompts, the agent's replies, and the conversation context.
  • Provider API keys you enter so fa can talk to your chosen AI provider (e.g. OpenRouter, Anthropic, or a custom endpoint).
  • Page content the agent reads when you ask it to act on a page (text, screenshots, cookies needed for the flow you drive, history/bookmark entries you explicitly reference).
  • Local files you attach or files the agent creates for you in its sandbox.
  • The developer receives none of the above. There is no telemetry or analytics in the browser extension at all; in the mobile/desktop app, optional Firebase analytics/crash reporting is described in section 2 and never includes message text, keys, or file contents.

2. How we handle data

  • On-device processing. Prompts, tool results, and files are processed on your device. Nothing is proxied through the developer: fa operates no servers that receive your conversation content, keys, or files.
  • AI requests. When you chat with the agent, the relevant prompt and context are sent — directly from your device — to the AI providers you configure (your keys, your base URLs). Those providers process your data under their own privacy policies.
  • Analytics (app only). Where the platform makes it available, the mobile/desktop app sends Firebase Analytics events with metadata only (event names, provider/model identifiers, coarse buckets) and Firebase Crashlytics crash reports (stack traces, device model, OS version) — never API keys, message text, prompts, or file contents. The browser extension sends no analytics and no crash reports.
  • Website analytics. The landing page (fa1.dev) uses Google Analytics 4 with IP anonymization to count page views and outbound clicks. It sets no advertising cookies and tracks nothing inside the app you run from the page.

3. Data storage

  • Everything fa keeps — chats, sessions, settings, provider keys, sandbox files — is stored locally on your device or in your browser: the platform Keychain / secure store for keys (app), chrome.storage and extension storage for extension state, OPFS/IndexedDB for web sandboxes and downloaded model caches.
  • Nothing is stored cloud-side by the extension or the developer. There is no fa account and no fa cloud.
  • On-device model files you choose to download (e.g. small LLM weights) are stored in your browser's storage and are never uploaded.

4. Data sharing

  • We do not sell your data, and we do not share it with third parties for marketing.
  • The only third parties that receive your content are the model providers you explicitly configure (your requests go directly to their endpoints).
  • Native messaging. When you pair the extension with a local fa CLI helper, the extension and that local helper exchange messages between themselves on your machine — this traffic does not involve the developer or any server.
  • Optional system permissions (notifications, microphone, calendar, contacts, health, home) are requested only in context for features you invoke, and the data they touch is processed on-device only.

5. Retention & deletion

  • Local data persists until you delete it: clear a chat/session inside the app, clear the extension's data via browser settings, or uninstall — uninstalling the app or extension removes its locally stored data.
  • Downloaded model weights and web-sandbox files live in your browser storage and can be cleared the same way (site data / extension data).
  • Firebase analytics/crash data (app only), where enabled, is retained per Google's standard Firebase retention and contains no message content.

6. Security

  • Keys. Provider API keys are stored in the platform Keychain (iOS/macOS) or the local secure store / browser storage of the app sandbox, and are transmitted only to the provider they belong to.
  • Redaction. A layered secret-redaction pipeline masks credentials and token-shaped strings in logs, session files, and tool output before they are persisted, so secrets do not leak into recorded sessions.
  • Approvals. Sensitive agent actions (running commands, opening pages, sending data out of the browser) pass an approval gate you control, from ask-per-action to fully unattended modes.
  • The extension loads all interpreter/LLM engine code from inside the package (no remotely hosted code), and its permissions are limited to what its features call.

7. Children's privacy

The app and the extension are not directed at children under 13 (or the equivalent minimum age in your jurisdiction), and we do not knowingly collect personal data from them.

8. Changes to this policy

Changes are posted at this URL with a new effective date.

  • October 15, 2026 — restructured into the nine Chrome Web Store mandatory sections; added the browser extension (local engine code, native messaging, no telemetry).
  • July 29, 2026 — first published version.

9. Contact

Questions, requests, or reports: open an issue at github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/issues.

Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,

callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. {"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the kept `is not defined` exemption can mask exactly the failure this checker now claims to catch**

The new comment says "any vendored-asset load failure is exactly what this checker exists to catch", but the filter one line down still exempts every error containing `is not defined`:

```dart
final fatal = errors.where((e) => !e.contains('is not defined'));
```

That is the signature failure of a vendored loader that did not install its global: if `vendor_loader_webllm.js` / `vendor_loader_transformers.js` fails before assigning `window.webllm` / `window.transformersjs` (or `m.Engine` comes back undefined for LiteRT), the Dart side's first touch logs `… is not defined` — silently downgraded to non-fatal. The PR's AC2 evidence for the three panel engines is only "panel renders + console fatal=0", so a silently degraded engine family would still pass this gate.

Note `litertLmReady` rejections are caught by design (the Dart side awaits and degrades), so a failed local import can be console-silent end-to-end.

Suggestions:
- assert the constructs explicitly: extend the panel probe/e2e to check `!!window.webllm`, `!!window.transformersjs`, and that `window.litertLmReady` settles fulfilled (all three are vendored and must load — that is the whole point of gh-1630), or
- narrow the exemption to the specific pre-gh-1630 benign source it was added for, so a missing engine global fails the checker.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the "re-fetching" path never re-fetches**

When a file exists in the vendor tree but its sha256 drifts from the lock (full mode), this line prints "re-fetching" — but control falls through to `verify(data)` on the **already-on-disk drifted bytes**, which can only fail the checksum and abort the build. No network fetch happens on this path (the `else` branch below is the only downloader, and it `continue`s past this code).

So the branch is: misleading log + a dead re-fetch intent + a trailing comment ("re-verify the written result too") that describes an outcome verify() can't produce here (if the bytes matched the pin we'd have `continue`d above). E1's fail-loud property is preserved — this is purely about the next person debugging a checksum mismatch wondering why "re-fetching" didn't fetch.

Either actually re-download on drift (delete the drifted file and take the `else` path), or reword the message to what happens ("…differs from the lock — refusing to ship unverified assets; delete `browser_ext/vendor/` and re-run").

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1631
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1631
- **Title**: gh-1630 [CWS REJECTION] fa — browser agent: vendor all CDN engines locally (keep every feature), drop 5 dead permissions, complete privacy policy — resubmission plan
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1630` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 59
- **Additions**: +3018
- **Deletions**: -618
- **Created**: 2026-10-15T12:40:53Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T07:18:22Z

## PR Description

Closes #1630
### Root Cause

The extension shipped remotely-hosted code: the panel app bundled the web
build's jsdelivr imports (on-device engines + the interpreters' CDN
constants in `main.dart.js`), and the offscreen runtimes rode unpinned
floating URLs with no re-verification. The manifest also declared five
permissions with zero call sites (`contentSettings`, `downloads`,
`fontSettings`, `identity`, `desktopCapture`) and a CSP without
`'wasm-unsafe-eval'`, and `site/privacy.html` missed six mandatory sections
in EN/RU — four independent rejection grounds, none addressed before
this fix.

### Previous Attempt

The previous dev leg (run 38722657674) failed without landing a fix — its
auto-save WIP commits net out to no diff vs main. Every rejection ground
was still open when this leg started.

### Fix

- `browser_ext/vendor.lock.json` + `scripts/fetch_vendor_assets.sh`: all six
  engines (quickjs, pyodide, sqljs, webllm, transformers, litert) pinned
  per-artifact with sha256 + version-pinned URLs; rewrites the bundled
  remote constants onto package-local dirs, re-verifies the tree on every
  build, generates the quickjs ffi-types shim.
- `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/web_interpreters_urls.dart` (new): the
  interpreters resolve per build via `--dart-define=FA_HOST=extension` —
  the extension compiles only `../../vendor/interpreters/...` paths; the
  CDN constants are tree-shaken out (verified on the compiled artifact:
  0 jsdelivr markers in `main.dart.js`). Pyodide now gets an explicit
  `indexURL` in both builds (no silent remote fallback).
- `scripts/stage_extension_panel.py` (new): replaces the panel's three CDN
  engine-loader tags (and their comments/orphaned modules) with
  `vendor_loader_*.js` importing from the package-local vendor dir — the
  on-device engines WORK in the extension now (the old stub disabled them).
- `browser_ext/manifest.json`: dead permissions removed; CSP is
  `'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'`.
- `site/privacy.html` + `PRIVACY.md`: nine mandatory sections (`data-sec`
  anchored) in EN and RU; store listing links the live URL.
- `scripts/check_cws_compliance.py` (new) + `ext_package_guard.py` remote
  scan: AC1 byte-scan of sources AND the built zip, manifest/privacy/lock
  asserts — wired into `.github/workflows/browser-ext.yml`, red blocks
  merge (REG-1).

### Test Coverage

- `test/browser_ext/cws_compliance_test.dart` (8), `test/site/privacy_policy_test.dart` (4),
  `flutter_app/test/web_interpreters_urls_test.dart` (3) — new; the
  compliance tests failed before the fix, pass after.
- Full suites: root dart 10,982 passed / 0 failed; browser_ext/dart 451;
  node 46; Playwright run-script (vendored quickjs + pyodide in the real
  extension) 6/6; panel-app e2e 2 passed (real app renders, no fatal
  overlay).

cp -R "flutter_app/build/web/canvaskit/." "browser_ext/panel/app/canvaskit/$REV/"
    for f in canvaskit.js canvaskit.wasm; do
      [ -f "browser_ext/panel/app/canvaskit/$REV/chromium/$f" ] || {
        echo "FATAL: canvaskit/$REV/chromium/$f missing after mirror" >&2
        exit 1
      }
    done
    echo "canvaskit mirrored to canvaskit/$REV/chromium/ (verified)"
    # canvaskit dedup (#1096 AC2): the engine only ever requests
    # canvaskit/<rev>/chromium/... (FLUTTER_WEB_CANVASKIT_URL=./canvaskit/
    # + the engineRevision the bootstrap pins), so the flat top-level
    # copy from build/web — canvaskit.js/wasm, chromium/, webparagraph/ —
    # is unreachable dead weight (~13MB duplicate subtree). Keep the rev
    # mirror (the verified-complete copy), drop its flat siblings.
    find browser_ext/panel/app/canvaskit -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 ! -name "$REV" -exec rm -rf {} +
    echo "canvaskit deduplicated to canvaskit/$REV/ (#1096)"
  else
    echo "FATAL: engineRevision not found in flutter_bootstrap.js" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  # The extension package must carry NO remote code (gh-1630 Blue Argon)
  # and its CSP forbids remote scripts: stage the on-device engine loaders
  # (WebLLM / transformers.js / LiteRT-LM) onto the package-local vendor
  # dir instead of the CDN imports the web build uses. Standalone,
  # idempotent script (test/browser_ext/cws_compliance_test.dart exercises
  # it) — replaces the pre-gh-1630 ondevice_stub.js failure shim: the
  # engines are vendored now, so they LOAD instead of degrading.
  python3 scripts/stage_extension_panel.py --app-dir browser_ext/panel/app
  echo "bundled fa web app (browser_ext/panel/app/)"
fi

# A staged app from an earlier --with-app run can outlive the flag (the
# dir is gitignored and never cleaned): without this, a plain local build
# zips panel/app/manifest.json verbatim and the guard fails the package
# (CWS single-manifest rule, #291). Strip unconditionally — idempotent.
if [ -d browser_ext/panel/app ]; then
  if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    python3 scripts/ext_package_guard.py strip browser_ext/panel/app
  else
    echo "WARNING: no python3 — cannot strip browser_ext/panel/app;" \
         "the packaging guard below hard-requires python3 anyway" >&2
  fi
fi

mkdir -p build
rm -f build/fa-extension.zip

# CWS-strict manifest (owner report 2026-10-11): the store uploader
# rejects // comments ("manifest.json:17:2: missing value") AND the dev
# "key" field ("key field is not allowed in manifest" — CWS owns the
# key, the source pins it only for a stable local dev id). The zip must
# carry a comment-stripped, key-less manifest while the source keeps
# both. Staged under build/pack/ so the zip entry name stays exactly
# "manifest.json". The ext_package_guard check below re-parses the
# packaged manifest STRICTLY and rejects "key", so a regression here
# fails the build, never the store upload.
mkdir -p build/pack
if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  python3 -c '
import json, re, sys
raw = open(sys.argv[1]).read()
m = json.loads(re.sub(r"^\s*//.*$", "", raw, flags=re.M))
m.pop("key", None)
open(sys.argv[2], "w").write(json.dumps(m, indent=2) + "\n")
' "$manifest" build/pack/manifest.json
elif command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  node -e 'const fs=require("fs"); const m=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(process.argv[1], "utf8").replace(/^\s*\/\/.*$/gm, "")); delete m.key; fs.writeFileSync(process.argv[2], JSON.stringify(m, null, 2) + "\n")' "$manifest" build/pack/manifest.json
else
  echo "WARNING: no python3/node — packaging the RAW source manifest;" \
       "the strict guard below is expected to fail (CWS needs stripped JSON)" >&2
  cp "$manifest" build/pack/manifest.json
fi

if command -v zip >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  runtime="sw content panel icons offscreen.html offscreen vendor"
  # panel/app rides inside the panel/ dir — no separate root entry.
  # The stripped CWS manifest rides from build/pack/ (the verbatim source
  # manifest.json stays out of the zip on purpose).
  ( cd browser_ext && zip -qr ../build/fa-extension.zip $runtime \
      -x 'sw/agent.js.map' 'sw/agent.js.deps' )
  ( cd build/pack && zip -q ../fa-extension.zip manifest.json )
else
python3 - <<'PY'
import os, zipfile
RUNTIME_DIRS = ("sw", "content", "panel", "icons", "offscreen", "vendor")
SKIP_NAMES = {"README.md", "agent.js.map", "agent.js.deps"}
with zipfile.ZipFile("build/fa-extension.zip", "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as z:
    # build/pack/manifest.json is the comment-stripped CWS copy made above.
    z.write("build/pack/manifest.json", "manifest.json")
    z.write("browser_ext/offscreen.html", "offscreen.html")
    for d in RUNTIME_DIRS:
